answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making every identity stake collateral at registration, routed through a bridge contract that verifies the deposit before minting credentials. The stake stays locked until settlement, so an alias that never clears grading forfeits it rather than profiting. A thousand phantom agents then demand a thousand funded stakes, which prices a flood attack out of reach for any attacker. Think of the atlas of identities: real agents hold actual capital, while fakes only add cost. Nothing survives long without that ember of real skin in the game.
